statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,127.16, down 241.28 points or 0.82%, after opening at 28,890.93 on a 1.63% gap below the 29,368.44 previous close. The session range was 28,867.67 to 29,285.50: the opening gap was roughly 71% recovered into the afternoon and then partly given back into the close, so both directional legs retraced inside the range and no persistent one-way structure was established. Nasdaq-100 futures trade near 29,452.75, about mid-range between the 29,107.25 low and the 29,604.50 high. Cross-asset amplifiers remain elevated but off their extremes: VIX settled at 17.11, up 8.02%, against an 18.17 session high; the 10-year yield is 4.961% and negative on the day after touching 5.012%; WTI is near 101.80 after a session high around 105. Tail is 19 and maps to the low band.
recommendation: Tail at 19 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is set at 13:00-15:00 UTC on 15 September, covering Tuesday's US cash open and the first full cash hour, where a second consecutive gap open after a chip-led decline and ahead of Wednesday's policy decision is the identified conditional risk. The conditional path stays in the low band through the CME maintenance halt, the post-halt reopen, the Asian session and the European morning, with small uplifts at the reopen, the Tokyo open and the European opening auction. It enters the watch band from 12:00 UTC and peaks at 22 at the cash open, then eases through the US afternoon with a further uplift around the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC and into the close. Stress remains high at 67 on an unresolved Middle East supply disruption, a 10-year yield that traded through 5%, and a policy decision on Wednesday that markets price as a near-certain 25 basis point increase. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unchanged by this assessment.
headline: NDX closes at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, with the 1.63% opening gap recovered to 29,285.50 and then partly given back; both legs retraced inside the session range, and with VIX off its 18.17 high and the 10-year negative on the day, Tail holds at 19 in the low band
body:
Monday resolved as a two-sided session rather than a directional one. The Nasdaq-100 cash index opened at 28,890.93, a 1.63% gap below the 29,368.44 previous close, traded down to 28,867.67, recovered roughly 71% of the gap to a 29,285.50 high, and then gave part of that back to settle at 29,127.16, down 241.28 points or 0.82%. The close sits in the lower half of the range but comfortably above the low. Both the recovery leg and the late fade retraced. That is the opposite of the structure that denies a reverse or grid approach the mean reversion it depends on, and it is the central reason Tail stays in the low band at the end of a day whose headline internals were severe.

Those internals were genuinely severe but narrow. The decline was concentrated in semiconductors after leaders at several US artificial-intelligence companies publicly called for a slower pace of model development: the PHLX chip index fell about 5.9%, with Micron off more than 5%, Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices each down more than 4%, and Nvidia down 3.4%. Against that, software and communication services traded higher, and the broader indices held up far better than the chip complex, with the S&P 500 down 0.48% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.56% against the Nasdaq-100's 0.82%. A rotation with one sector under heavy pressure and others bid is a dispersion event, not a liquidation, and dispersion of that kind raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than establishing a one-way index path.

The cross-asset stack is the reason Stress stays high at 67. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, with a design capacity around 7 million barrels per day, remains shut after drone attacks, Strait of Hormuz transit has fallen to very low levels, and Iran-GCC talks scheduled in Oman were postponed. Brent traded above $109 and WTI reached roughly $105 before easing to about $101.80. The 10-year Treasury yield traded through 5% for the first time since 2023 before settling at 4.961%, negative on the day, and US diesel set a record. Markets now price a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's policy meeting as close to certain. Each of these is a live source of gap and repricing risk, and together they justify a high Stress reading. None of them is the same thing as observed persistent directional efficiency in the index itself, which is what Tail measures, and the amplifiers that would have mattered most all closed off their extremes: VIX at 17.11 against an 18.17 high, crude off its high, the long end reversing its move through 5%.

The forward path therefore stays in the low band through the CME maintenance halt and the thin overnight window, with small conditional uplifts at the post-halt reopen and the Tokyo open, where Middle East supply news has repriced first on recent sessions. It crosses into the watch band from 12:00 UTC on Tuesday and peaks at 22 across the 13:00-15:00 UTC cash open, which forms the danger window. A second consecutive gap open followed by continuation with only shallow pullbacks is the specific configuration that would change the assessment; an open that is absorbed inside Monday's range would confirm the current reading. Wednesday's policy decision falls outside this 24-hour window and is carried in the event calendar.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series began in the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band at 21:00 UTC as the AI-slowdown story and the Middle East supply disruption developed, and held the watch band through the overnight and Asian sessions. It reached the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows under a trend-down mode, eased to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, and returned to the elevated band at 13:00 UTC as the first bounce faded into the cash open. From 14:00 UTC the series eased steadily as the opening gap was absorbed, reaching 18 and the low band at 16:00 UTC, returning to 21 at 17:00 and 18:00 UTC on successive new session highs, and easing to 19 at 19:00 UTC once the high stopped being exceeded. Stress fell continuously from a 79 peak to 68 by 19:00 UTC, and Confidence held between 87 and 89 across the whole US session.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built on a completed two-sided session: a 1.63% opening gap that was roughly 71% recovered and then partly given back, with both legs retracing inside a 28,867.67 to 29,285.50 range, and with VIX, the 10-year and crude all settling off their session extremes. Conditional Tail holds at 19 for the post-close hour, falls to 17 across the CME maintenance halt, and returns to 19 at the post-halt reopen where thin liquidity makes the first prints the main gap-risk point. It settles between 17 and 19 across the Asian session with a small uplift at the Tokyo open, where Middle East supply news has repriced first, then lifts to 19 at the European opening auction and holds in the low band through the European morning. The path crosses into the watch band at 12:00 UTC ahead of the Empire State survey and reaches its maximum of 22 at Tuesday's 13:00 UTC cash open, easing to 21 in the following hour; those two hours form the danger window. It then eases through the US afternoon, with an uplift to 20 around the 17:00 UTC 20-year bond auction and again into the 19:00 UTC close as positioning ahead of Wednesday's policy decision builds. A second consecutive gap open followed by continuation without a meaningful retracement is the specific path that would invalidate this outlook.
